8. 0 PROCESSES

8.1.1 Surgery: -Treatment Manual

8.1. 2 Agni karma

In Ayurveda, various modalities of treatments are given but Agnikarma is supposed to give instant relief from pain. Pain is the chief cause of visiting a doctor in most patients. It is known as Ruja which is one of the synonyms of many surgical diseases. In today's era quick pain relief is of prime importance to resume normal activities. Hence Agnikarma (therapeutic intentional burn) is considered as instant healers of pain.

IMPORTANCE OF AGNIKARMA

1. It is a highly potential procedure than the bheshaja, Shastra &ksharakarma.

2. It is very effective to terminate the chance of recurrence of the disease.

3. No infection.

4. No secondary complication if done properly.

MATERIALS REQUIRED

1. Agnikarma Shalaka

2. Permanent Marker

3. Gas stove, lighter

4. Surgical spirit , Gloves

5. Cotton gauze

6. Haridra Churna (turmeric), Aloe vera pulp

REQUIREMENTS: INFRASTRUCTURE FACILITIES AND MANPOWER:

Manpower:

• A trained doctor and technician

Space and requirements:

• 1 small sized room (10x 10) with proper light. It can be done in OPD level also

• Chair or stool- 1

• Examination table/ Droni- 1.

Preoperative:

1. Educate the patient

2. Obtain informed consent

3. Ask the patient to satisfy natural urges

4. Check vitals

AGNIKARMA PROCEDURE:

1. The patient should be allowed to be in a comfortable position, exposing the site of the problem.

2. Keep Shalaka in the gas stove for heating.

3. Wear surgical gloves.

4. Clean the site with the surgical spirit or Murivenna oil.

5. Mark the tender most points with a marker.

6. Ensure Shalaka to be red hot.

7. Hold red hot Shalaka strongly in one hand and touch in the marked points for upto 2-3 seconds only (depends on the site and tenderness).

POST OPERATIVE CARE

1. Keep Shalaka in the specified place.

2. Apply Aloe vera pulp over the Agnikarma site. Wait for a while and then apply Haridra churna with cotton over there.

APPLICATION & DURATION

▪ It depends up on site & disease

▪ Usually 2 to 5 seconds & more than 5 seconds in corn, callosity etc.

▪ The effect of Agnikarma on mamsa dhatu will reach into sira, snayu, asthi& sandhi.

TIME / SEASON

All seasons except Greeshma & Sharat Ritu. In the case of an emergency, it can be done in any season with special precautions.

PRECAUTIONS

1. Agnikarma should not be done on an empty stomach. It is better to take Pichchila anna before Agnikarma.

2. Should be aware of vital parts of the body, season, vyadhi dhoshaavastha.

3. Care should be taken while heating Shalaka and placing it in a specified place after Agnikarma.

8.1.3 RAKTAMOKSHANA

Introduction

Raktamoksha is a technical word comprising Rakta (blood) and Moksha (to expel), which means the process in which the vitiated blood is expelled out of the body. In general we translate Raktamokshana as bloodletting. It is withdrawal of blood to cure or prevent an illness. There are various methods to conduct Raktamokshana.

They are-

• Siravedha (venipuncture)

• Prachhana (bloodletting by pricking),

• Jalauka avacharana (application of leeches),

• Shringaavacharana (bloodletting using horn) and Alabuavacharana (bloodletting using bottle gourd).

Now modified modern equipment is being used as an alternative to Shringa and Alabu. The theory put forward in the choice of the correct method of Raktamokshana is based upon the predominance of vitiated doshas. According to the vitiated doshas the Shringa (horn) is used in conditions where blood is vitiated by Vata, because it is snigdha (unctuous). Jalauka (leech) being sheet (cold), it is used in Pitta vitiated condition and Alabu (bottle gourd) is used in Kapha dominance because it is Rooksha (dry). Prachhana is indicated when doshas are localized and pindita (collected). Shiravedhan is indicated in Tridoshaj (vitiation of all doshas)

REQUIREMENT INFRASTRUCTURE FACILITIES AND MANPOWER

Manpower:

• A trained doctor and technician

Space and requirements:

• 1 small sized room (10x 10) with proper light. It can be done at the OPD level also.

• Chair or stool- 1

• Examination table- 1.

Duration

Once and may be repeated after an interval of 7 days, 15 days, 30 days or 45 days.

Indications

Raktamokshana is very much useful in diseases like skin diseases (scabies, erysipelas, blemishes etc), filariasis, non-healing wounds, varicose vein, high BP, frozen shoulder, sciatica, acute inflammation etc.

Contraindications

Raktamokshana techniques like shiravedha and prachchhana are avoided in children and cowardly patients. Some diseases like anemia, diabetes, bleeding disorders like hemophilia etc. are contraindicated for Raktamokshana.

PROCEDURE

The procedure is divided into 3 parts

1. Purva karma (Pre-operative procedure)In the preoperative procedure. Snehana (oleation) internal and external, swedana(hot fomentation with steam to whole body).

2.Pradhan Karma(operative procedure) .

a) By using Jalauka(leeach)

The patient is made to lie on the bed comfortably. The leach is applied over the affected part. The leech starts to suck blood when its mouth becomes raised and appears like a horse's hoof. If the leech does not suck blood a drop of milk is put at the spot or a small prick with sterilized needle is taken. A wet cotton is kept over the body of the leech to keep it moist and alive. The leech leaves the spot after a while or is deliberately removed when the patient experiences pricking pain at the site. (This pain indicates that the Leach is sucking pure blood).

b)siravedha (venous puncture)

The patient is asked to lie comfortably over a bed. The air cuff of the sphygmomanometer is tied over the bicep muscle of the hand. The patient is asked to clench his fist tightly. The cuff is inflated and the desired vein(medial cubital is preferred) is punctured with a sterilized scalp vein(butterfly) needle. The cuff is removed and the blood is collected in a kidney tray. When the sufficient quantity of blood is drawn the needle is withdrawn and the patient is asked to loosen his fist. A cotton swab is pressed over the wound.

3. Paschat karma (post-operative procedure)

If bleeding continues from the diseased site, fine powders of lodhra (Symplocos racemosa), yastimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra),raktachandana (Pterocarpus Santalinus) etc. are applied. The area covered is wet cloth or a thin paste of cooling dravya like chandan is applied.The patient is advised to take rest and can be given light diet or milk later in the evening. Rice flour is applied to the whole body of Jalauka and little siandhava lavana (rock salt) and oil is applied to its mouth. And it is squeezed gently from tail to mouth in order to remove the sucked blood. Now Jalauka is immersed in water and can be used after a span of seven days.

Investigations required before raktamokshan-

• Hb%

• HIV

• HBSAg

• CT

• BT

8.2 Procedures: Shalakya Tantra

8.2.1 NETRA KRIYAKALPA: Shalakya Tantra is one among & Specialties of Ashtang Ayurveda which deals with the diseases occurring above the clavicle, so it mainly deals with the sense organs diseases affecting them & their management. As the panchakarma is the base of Kayachikitsa, Netrakiryakalpa is the main therapeutics procedure for Ophthalmic patients in Shalakya Tantra. ‘Kriya’ means therapeutic procedures, used to cure diseases and ‘Kalpa’ means specific formulation used for therapy, in Ayurvedic Ophthalmology. It includes selection of specific procedures, preparations of special drug form and finally its proper application to the eyes.

Types of Kriyakalpa –

NETRATARPANA- Tarpana is indicated in Vata-pitta dominating personalities suffering from eye diseases. Procedure –

• The patient is asked to lie down in supine position.

• A circular wall of black gram paste is made around the eyes.

• Medicated ghee like Triphala, Yashtimadhu or other medication is used after autoclaving and liquefaction. It is poured into the eyes with all aseptic precautions.

• Patients are asked to blink the eyes for specific period of time around 15 to 30 minutes, according to stage, severity of diseases & prakriti of patients.

• After that, medicated ghee is removed with the help of a syringe and wall of black gram is also removed.

• Eyes cleaned with lukewarm water with help of sterile cotton.

Indication: Healthy person, dry eyes & computer vision syndrome, high myopia, all Drishtigata vyadhi, presbyopia, diabetic retinopathy and posterior segment ailments.

Contraindications - Acute conjunctivitis, Active eye infections, corneal ulcer, Recent ocular surgery, Allergy to herbal/ghee preparations.

Reference: Sushrut Uttartantra Chapter 18. Dalhan's commentary by P.V.Sharma, Choukhamba vishwa bharati, oriental publishers, Varanasi reprint- Year 2011, ISBN- 978-81-909871

Scientific approach: Eye Ointment and gels used in Modern sciences can be co-related with Netra tarpana. Netra tarpana is one such ocular therapy where tissue contact time is more due to the lipophilic & hydrophilic nature of the drug. Large size molecules can also pass through the epithelium as its used preparation is in aqueous suspension form. So it will cross corneal epithelium barrier easily. Due to more tissue contact time active components of the drug will be absorbed more. Scope– Tarpan can be used in Drishtigata vyadhi like refractive error, myopia, Diabetic Retinopathy, ARMD, Hypertensive Retinopathy, Computer vision syndrome, dry eye syndrome, blurred vision and ptosis.

1) ASCHYOTANA: It is also one of the ocular Ayurvedic therapeutics where decoction of raw drugs is used. The active principle is aqueous extract.

Procedure: Ashchyotana means medicated eye drop instilled into the eyes at a certain distance 2 angul (7 to 8 cm) from the eyeball. Decoction of raw drugs is instilled into the eyes.

1. Preparation of Decoction:

• Select suitable raw herbal drugs based on the condition.

• Prepare a fresh aqueous decoction using induction heating.

• Filter the decoction through a fine cotton cloth or sieve.

2. Patient Preparation:

• Make the patient lie comfortably on the wooden examination table.

• Clean the eyes using sterile gauze if needed.

3. Administration:

• Using a sterile dropper, instill the decoction from a height of about 2 angula (approximately 7–8 cm).

• Avoid contact with the dropper with the eye or lashes.

• Allow 2–3drops in each eye.

• Instruct the patient to gently blink and keep the eyes closed for a few seconds.

4. Post-ProcedureCare:

• Monitor for any immediate reactions or discomfort.

• Repeat 3–4 times a day or as per disease severity.

Indication: First line of treatment in all eye diseases like conjunctivitis, corneal ulcer to glaucoma, other inflammatory and degenerative eye diseases.

Scope – It is used as a first line treatment in all eye disorders, almost in all ocular or eye diseases.

Scientific approach: It is like eye drops used by Modern ophthalmologists. In Ayurved fresh decoction of raw drug is made & filtered & to be instilled into the eyes 3-4 times or frequently as per the severity of the eye diseases & according to symptoms. The active principle is aqueous extract. Tissue contact time is very less. It gets diluted with the tears and drained into Naso-lacrimal duct.

Reference: Sushrut Uttartantra Chapter 18. Dalhan’s commentary by P.V.Sharma, Choukhamba Vishwa bharati, oriental publishes, Varanasi reprint- Year 2011, ISBN- 978-81- 909871

2) PUTAPAKA

Procedure: Two lumps of finely pounded meat each weighing 40gm, drugs 40 gm and liquids one kudav- all mixed together are wrapped with leaves, pasted with soil and heated on burning charcoal of khadira wood. After steaming, squeeze the liquid out and instill it in the inner canthus while the patient is lying down. Putapaka is mainly done after Tarpana.

A. Preparation Phase:

• Clean and disinfect the working area.

• Mix:

- 2 lumps of 40 gm pounded meat

- 40gm of prescribed herbal drugs

- 1Kudva of liquid

• Wrap the mixture in green leaves (e.g, castor leaves).

• Cover the wrapped bundle with mud to create a sealed ball.

B. Heating Phase:

• Place the prepared bundle on Khadira charcoal.

• Allow it to heat until steaming is complete (approx.20–30minutes).

C. Administration Phase:

• Remove the bundle and let it cool slightly.

• Squeeze out the liquid into a clean sterile container.

• With the patient lying supine, instill the warm liquid into the inner canthus of both eyes.

• Ensure eyes remain closed for a few minutes post-instillation.

Requirement like Tarpana

Plant extract after close chamber, ball wrapped by green leaves like castor leaf & layer of mud and combustion.

Indication/Scope- It is indicated when the eye gets fatigued after Tarpana, i.e for rejuvenation of eyes. Putapaka is used to give energy to the eyes to overcome fatigue.

Contraindications: Acute eye infections, Eye trauma, Allergy to any ingredients.

Scientific approach- Used preparation is in aqueous solution form and active component concentration is high. Tissue contact time is very less. Used after Tarpana to increase drashti bala to strengthen the eyes & in mild eye affections.

Responsibility:

• Ophthalmologist or Shalakya consultant -1

• Therapist-1

3) ANJANA

Ayurvedic ocular therapeutic liniment of drugs. Bioavailability is more due to more tissue contact time.

Type & procedure:

• Lekhana, ropana & prasudanna collyrium

• Scraping collyrium by its potency, drains out dosh, situated in vessels, sacs & channels of eyelids and also in shringataka marma through mouth, nostrils and eyes.

• Collyrium is of 3 types- Rods, semisolid and powder.

• By measurement, varti (gutika-rod) for scrapping should be equal to harenu (pea), for purifying equal to one & half harenu.

• Collyrium should be mixed with ghee & with the help of a rod made of Suvarna and tamra applied on the palpebral conjunctiva.

• The careful physician holding the eye oblique with his left hand should apply collyrium at the inner canthus also moving it to & for application on eyelids however should be done with the finger itself.

Requirements:

• 200sqft rooms examination table

• induction

• spirit lamp

• small vessels

• container to keep anjana material, copper/steel/iron or gold accordingly.

• Rods – Gold, iron, tamra

• different chakshushya (netra) dravya

• Collyrium rods – Bud shaped at both ends thick as pea, eight fingers in length, thin in centre & well finished & easy to handle. It should be made of copper, stone etc.

Staff

• Ophthalmologist or Shalakya consultant -1

• Therapist-1

Scientific approach- Bioavailability is more due to more tissue contact time.

Indications / Scope – Anjanas are mainly Lekhana properties which can gradually taper the thickness of the membrane and thereby prevent the growth and also reduces size.It is indicated in Pterygium, Conjunctival disorder, early stage of cataract, glaucoma. Pakshmaghata, an eye disorder, not only in diseased eyes but useful in normal healthy eyes. It has direct action on ocular tissues especially on Conjunctiva, so it is useful in Conjunctival disorder. It flushes out debris and unwanted tissue due to its Lekhana property. Nasya, Seka, Pindi & Shirodhara have the same requirements.

4) NETRAPARISHEK –

Procedure –Ayurvedic ocular therapeutic procedure involving the continuous pouring of medicated liquid over the eyes. It helps in soothing, cleansing and revitalizing the ocular tissues, ensuring enhanced bioavailability due to prolonged tissue contact.

Type & Procedure:

Netra parishek is primarily Snehana (lubricating), Shodhana (purifying) and Ropana (healing) in nature. The medicated liquid (decoction or herbal extracts) is poured in a thin stream over the closed eyes from a height of approximately 4 angul. It aids in removing toxins, alleviating dryness, soothing irritation and nourishing the eyes. The process is repeated for a specific duration as per the condition and consultants advice. The liquid should be lukewarm and poured continuously in an arrhythmic manner to avoid sudden shocks to the eyes. The therapy should be performed in a calm, well ventilated environment to maximize its effects.

Requirements:

• 200 sq.ft. examination room with a comfortable table for the patient to lie down.

• Induction heater or a controlled heating source to maintain the temperature of the liquid.

• Spirit lamp for sterilizing tools.

• Small vessels for preparing and pouring the medicated liquid.

• Container to hold and store medicated liquid (preferably made of copper, steel, iron or gold

• Rods & Equipment: Gold, iron, tamarods and different Chakshushya (ocularbeneficial) drugs.

Scientific Approach: Bio-availability is enhanced due to the prolonged contact time between the medicated liquid and ocular tissues. Ensures deep penetration of medicinal properties into ocular channels (srotas) for enhanced healing.

Indications/Scope: Useful in dry eye syndrome, conjunctival irritation, computer vision syndrome, early-stage cataract, glaucoma and post-surgical eye care. Has a cooling, nourishing and detoxifying effect on the ocular tissues. This reduces burning sensation, foreign body sensation and visual fatigue. It is also effective in both diseased and healthy eyes for preventive and curative purposes.

Staff Requirement:

• Ophthalmologist or Shalakya consultant - 1

• Therapist – 1

5) BIDALAKA –

Bidalaka provides externalocular therapy for various disorders by applying medicated paste over the eyelids, aiming to relieve inflammation, swelling and irritation using Ayurvedic principles.

Procedure –

Preparation Phase:

•Select appropriate herbal powder based on condition.

•Mix with sterile water or rose water to form a smooth paste.

•Make the patient lie down or sit comfortably with head support.

•Clean the peri orbital region with sterile cotton.

Execution Phase:

•Apply the paste evenly over the closed eyelids (avoid eyeball contact).

•Leave the paste undisturbed for15–30 minutes.

•Ensure the patient is calm and eyes remain closed during the procedure.

Post-procedure Phase:

•Gently remove the paste using moist cotton.

•Clean the area with rose water or sterile water.

•Instruct patients to avoid screen use for a few hours.

Scientific Basis – Bidalak works through transdermal absorption of herbal actives over eyelids. Cooling, anti-inflammatory and soothing properties of herbs relieve eye fatigue, irritation and superficial inflammation, acting similarly to anti-inflammatory eye ointments and cold compresses in modern medicine.

Scope –

This SOP applies to Ayurvedic Eye Care Units and Panchakarma Centres where Bidalak is indicated for:

•Inflammatory eye conditions

•Conjunctivitis

•Blepharitis

•Eye strain

•Burning sensation in the eyes

•Swelling and pain around the eyes

6) KARNA POORANA

Procedure –

Karnapoorana is an Ayurvedic therapeutic procedure that involves instilling or pouring medicated oil or liquid into the ear canal. It is designed to nourish, cleanse, and pacify the ear structures and is useful both in preventive and curative approaches.

Type & Procedure:

• Sneha Karna poorana: Involves pouring warm medicated oils into the ear canal.

• Kashaya Karna-poorana : Involves decoctions or other aqueous herbal preparations.

• The patient is made to lie in a lateral position with the affected ear facing upwards.

• The medicated oil or decoction is warmed to body temperature and gently poured drop by drop or in a stream into the ear canal using a sterile dropper or small funnel.

• The liquid is retained for a specific period (usually5–10minutes) as per the physician’s direction.

• The ear is then wiped gently with sterile cotton.

• The procedure is repeated for the opposite ear if needed.

Requirements:

• 100–150 sqft clean and ventilated room.

• Comfortable examination table or reclining chair.

• Induction heater or water bath to warm oil/decoction.

• Spirit lamp for sterilizing instruments.

• Sterile droppers, small funnels, cotton swabs and towels. Containers (glass, copper or steel) for storing oils or decoctions.

• Medicated oils or decoctions like Bilva taila, Anu taila, Eranda taila or as per condition.

Scientific Approach: Prolonged contact of medicated liquid with the auditory canal promotes deeper absorption and therapeutic effect. Helps to balance Vata dosha, especially in the head and neck region. It also acts on the auditory nerves and tissues, offering soothing, anti-inflammatory and rejuvenating effects.

Indications/Scope:

• Tinnitus (Karna nada)

• Earache(Karnashoola)

• Excessive ear wax

• Hearing loss (Badhirya)

• Vertigo and imbalance due to Vata disorders

Preventive care in high-noise environments or frequent exposure to wind and cold

Staff Requirement:

• Ayurvedic ENT/Shalakya Consultant -1

• Therapist – 1

8) KARNA DHOOPAN

Karnadhoopan is a classical Ayurvedic therapy indicated for various disorders of the ear, especially those arising due to Kapha-Vata dosha vitiation. This procedure involves fumigation of the external auditory canal using medicated smoke derived from herbs with antimicrobial, antifungal and anti-inflammatory properties.

Procedure:

The patient is made to sit in a comfortable upright or slightly reclined position. A herbal dhoopan stick (ear fumigation stick) or medicated dhoop prepared from ingredients like Guggulu, Vacha, Neem, Haridra, and Nimba patra is ignited, and the medicated smoke is allowed to enter the external auditory canal using a funnel or ear cone for a specific duration (1–2minutes per ear). Care is taken to ensure the heat does not harm the delicate ear structures.

Indications:

• Karṇasūla (earache)

• Karṇanāda (tinnitus)

• Badhirya (hearing impairment)

• Fungal infections

• Otorrhoea (ear discharge)

• Ear wax blockage

• Otitis externa

• As a preventive care in cold-prone individuals

Reference:

Ashtanga Hridaya Uttaratantra Chapter 19 : Sharangadhara Samhita Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India; Vaidya Yoga Ratnavali Commentaries by Kaviraj Atridev Gupta and Dr.P.V.Sharma Chaukhambha Sanskrit Series

Scientific Approach:

Karna dhoopan is comparable to modern aerosolized anti septic and anti fungal ear therapies. The volatile oils and antimicrobial phytoconstituents from the herbs enter the external auditory canal and act against local infections. The warmth from the smoke helps liquefy. Impacted cerumen and improves local circulation which enhances drug absorption. It may also provide symptomatic relief from tinnitus and ear congestion.

Scope:

• Otomycosis (fungal infections)

• Wax impaction

• Early-stage otitis externa

• Tinnitus

• Cold-related ear discomfort

• As an adjunct therapy post ear surgeries for antiseptic action (only under expert supervision)

Requirements:

• Herbal dhoopan sticks (containing Guggulu,Vacha, Nimba, Haridra etc.)

8.3 PANCHAKARMA PROCEDURES

A. SNEHANA (INTERNAL OLEATION)

Introduction: - Snehana stands for oleation of the whole body by the administration of fatty substances (oils and ghrita) internally and externally. Snehapana (internal administration of Sneha-oils and ghrita) is an important preparatory procedure for Panchakarma. Four main types of Snehana dravyas are mentioned in the classics viz. Ghrita (Ghee), Taila (Oil), Vasa (Fat) and Majja (bone marrow). Out of these Ghrita is considered as the best because of its properties. Snehana (Oleation) includes:

• Abhyantara Snehana (Internal Oleation)

• Bahya Snehana (External Oleation)

Abhyantara Snehana: Internal oleation classified into Achchha Pana (only snehanana dravya) and Vicharana snehana (snehana dravya mixed with food)

Achchha Pana: Oral administration of medicated Sneha (Ghee / oil) without mixing with food or other medicinal preparations and used for the purpose of oleation and lubrication of body tissues prior to the Shodhana therapy.

Requirement

Requirement-Manpower

a. Ayurvedic Physician: 1Attendant/ Nurse: 1

b. Requirement-Material

c. Medicated ghee or oil according to the requirement

d. Measuring glass

e. Saindhava (Rock Salt)

f. Hot water for drinking (boiled with Shunthi+Dhanyaka)

g. Panchatikta Ghrita, Indukanta Ghrita, Mahatiktaka Ghrita, Sukumara Ghrita, Masha taila, Dhanwantara Taila, Ksheera Bala Taila etc.

2. Pre operative

• Agnibala (digestive power) and Koshta ( ) assessment should be done in the patient prior to Snehapana.

• For the patient with unknown doshas, agni etc. one may start with Hrasiyasi matra (which is digested within two yamas/hours).

3. Operative

• The patient who is intended to undergo Snehapana is to take the Sneha early in the morning (within 15 minutes of sunrise) in the prescribed dose based on his Agnibala (digestive capacity), nature of disease, condition of body etc.

• The usual dosage is between 30 to 50 ml for Ghrita and 20 to 30 ml for Taila on the first day. • The dose for the next day should be fixed after assessing the time taken for digestion and agnipradurbhava.

• Snehapana (internal administration of unctuous substance) may be continued till Samyaka Snigdha Lakshanas (symptoms of desired effect) are observed and usually it is obtained within 3 to 7 days. Usual practice of increasing order of

• Snehapana dosage:

First day : 30ml

Second day: 60ml

Third day : 90ml

Fourth day : 120ml

Up to 7thday :210ml

4. Post operative

• Hot water and yusha (gruel) is given in small doses to enhance digestion (Deepana, Pachana).

• The patient is advised to avoid ashtomahadoshakar bhava.

• Avoid day sleep

• Avoid travelling and direct contact with air

5. Safety Precautions

• Care should be taken to avoid excessive heating of sneha dravya

6. Emergency Management

• Indigestion, Vomiting, Nausea, Anorexia, Headache, Constipation etc.

VASTI (MEDICATED ENEMA)

1. Introduction

Vastikarma is the procedure by which the medicines in suspension form are administered through rectum or genitourinary tract using Vastiyantra (Specific apparatus). It is the most important procedure among Panchakarma procedures and the most appropriate remedial measure for Vatadosha. It is called half treatment in Panchakarma

2. Requirement

a. Requirement-Manpower Ayurvedic Physician:1, Masseur:1

b. Requirement-Material

• Vastiputaka (polythene bag/ Enema pot approx. 1.5 Lt. capacity) – 1

• Vasti netra (Nozzle)- 1 Lavatory facilities

• Others (thread, vessels, churner, heating apparatus, table/ bench, towel, hot water for bath etc.)

• Medicated oils for Abhyanga

• Swedana Karma materials

• Medicated oils for Vasti

• Kwatha (Decoction) & Kalka (Paste) made from prescribed medicines –

• Madhu (Honey)

• Saindhava (Rock-salt)

3. Pre operative- For Niruha vasti (Decoction enema)-

• Sarwanga or sthanik abhyanga and swedana

• The niruhabasti is given before meals (i.e. 8-9 AM). It consist of Medicated oil or ghee -60ml, Madhu- 45ml, decoction of prescribed drugs- 300ml, Satavaha kalka-7.5gm, rock salt-4 gm

• Preparation of Vasti dravya- Powdered rock-salt is added to honey and stirred in a clean vessel with a pestle. Luke worm oil is added to this mixture little by little and again stirred. Then paste of Shatahwa followed by decoction is to be added little by little and mixed properly to make homogenous emulsion, and heated gently in a water bath (slightly above body temperature). The mixture gets filtered from the filter. This mixture is poured into a Vastiputaka (polythene bag/processed animal bladder/Enema Pot) and fixed with Vasti Netra (tied by using thread).

For Sneha Vasti (Oil Enema)

• Sarwanga or sthanik abhyanga and swedana

• It is given just after meals

• It includes the ingredients like medicated oil- 240ml saindhav-5gm, Satavaha kalka-5gm

• Mix the above mentioned drug in a proper manner to prepare in emulsified form

4. Operative:- For Niruha Vasti

• After Abhyanga and Swedana, the patient is advised to lie down in the left lateral position. Little quantity of oil is applied on the patient's anus and nozzle of Vasti yantra. The nozzle is gently inserted into the anal canal up to a specific length and Vastiputaka containing mixture is pressed with a uniform pressure. The pressure is continued till only a small quantity of fluid remains in the bag (to avoid air insertion). Then the nozzle is removed gently and the patient is allowed to lie down on the supine position till he feels the urge to excrete. The Vasti dravya, along with faeces, normally comes out within 10 minutes when a full dose of Niruha Vasti is given. The maximum time specified for retention of Vasti dravya is 48 minutes. After evacuation of the bowel, the patient may take a hot water bath and a semi-solid diet. Usually, Niruha Vastis are not to be given alone. Wherever required, Niruha Vasti must be given alternatively with Sneha Vasti.

• Arrangement of Sneha Vastis in the beginning, NiruhaVastis and Sneha Vastis alternatively later followed by Sneha Vastis in the last is done in three specific patterns according to total number of Vastis, the severity of disease and condition of the patient etc. These are known as:

o Karma Vasti :- 30 in number (12 Niruha, 18 Anuvasana)

o Kala Vasti:- 16 in number (6 Niruha, 10 Anuvasana)

Yoga Vasti:- 8 in number (3 Niruha, 5 Anuvasana).

5. Operative for Sneha Vasti:-

• After Abhyanga and Swedana, the patient is advised to lie down in the left lateral position. The Vastidravya (Sneha) is administered in a similar manner as Niruha vasti. As it is a retention enema, the contents should be allowed to retain inside for a minimum period of nine hours and all efforts are to be done for the same. It is not harmful even though it is retained for one day.

6. Post operative

• Niruha vasti - after defecation patients have to take bath followed by light food.

• Anuvasana /sneha vasti – head low position, tap buttock 3 times , massage palm and soles, anticlock wise massage over abdomen.

7. Safety Precautions

• Care should be taken while inserting vastinetra in anus.

• Observation of Niruha vasti pratyagamana kala (45 min to 1 hour)

8. Emergency Management: -

These may result into various complications like:

• Local anal injury

• GIT symptoms like pain in abdomen, vomiting etc.

• Very rarely generalized symptoms like murchha (syncope), angamarda (bodyache) etc.Management is done accordingly

UTTARBASTI (Insertion of Medicated oil, decoction into Intra Uterine Cavity through Vagina)

The standard Operating Procedure of Uttarbasti can be explained as follows

A) Uttarbastiin vaginal condition

• Vaginal infections – Bacterial and fungal infections are commonly found in vagina.

• Drugs used for these conditions should be bactericidal or bacteriostatic or antifungal in nature.

• Vaginal Mucosal defects – The vaginal mucosal defects may be explained under the following headings.

• Vaginal milieu pH.

Generally vaginal PH remains in between 3 & 4.This acidic PH prevents vaginal infections. In case of PH variations appropriate drugs should be administered to restore normal PH.

Time of administration

• Before administration of Uttarbasti previous infections should be cleared thoroughly.

• It should be administered after cleansing of a woman's body by two or three AsthapanaBasties, It should be administered preferably during Artavakalaor Ritukala(Just after menstrual bleeding is over). Basti Dravya Kashaya (decoction), Taila (oil) and only oil/kashay are used simultaneously as basti dravya for Niruha, Anuvasana and Uttarbasti respectively.

Method of Uttarbasti Administration

The female patient should be in positioned supine posture with flexed thighs and elevated knees. The nozzle should be inserted in the urinary or vaginal passage slowly with steady hands following the direction of the passage. In day and night i.e. in 24 hours total two, Three or four bastis should be given. Procedure should be continued for three nights (day and night) with gradual increase in oleaginous substance. After giving rest for three days, the procedure should be repeated for another three days.

Practical/ Procedure of Uttarbasti

Requirements

Instruments:
